chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it (to the Imam), said:

The Sunnah regarding the embalming (camphor) is thirteen dirhams and a third, at most. And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) descended unto the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with embalming, and its weight was forty dirhams. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) divided it into three parts: a part for himself, a part for Ali, and a part for Fatima (peace be upon her).'

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ دِرْهَمًا: Forty dirhams (a measure of weight/value for the camphor)
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: The recommended prophetic practice or tradition
key_terms.الْحَنُوطِ: Camphor or a mixture used for embalming the deceased
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: A unit of weight or currency used in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended amount of camphor for washing the deceased according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the recommended quantity of camphor (hanoot) for washing the deceased, citing a prophetic precedent where the Angel Jibra'il delivered forty dirhams' worth, which the Prophet divided equally among himself, Imam Ali, and Sayyida Fatima. This equal distribution underscores the spiritual parity and shared status of the Ahl al-Bayt in ritual purity, while the specific measurement reflects the practical jurisprudence (fiqh) of the time regarding burial rites.
